title: Matthew Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 8.

questions.question: In Matthew 8, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: A leper worshipped Jesus and asked to be made clean
Jesus put forth his hand and touched the leper
Jesus came down from the mountain and great multitudes followed him
A centurion came to Jesus beseeching him
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus came down from the mountain and great multitudes followed him
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:1 states that Jesus came down from the mountain and great multitudes followed him, which is the earliest event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: Who came to Jesus and worshipped him, saying, 'Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean'?
options: A leper
A centurion
A blind man
A Pharisee
questions.correctAnswer: A leper
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:2 states that a leper came and worshipped Jesus, asking to be made clean.

questions.question: What did Jesus do to the leper to make him clean?
options: He put forth his hand and touched him
He spoke a word from afar
He sent him to the priests
He laid hands on him without touching
questions.correctAnswer: He put forth his hand and touched him
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:3 states that Jesus put forth his hand and touched the leper, saying 'I will; be thou clean.'

questions.question: What did Jesus instruct the cleansed leper to do after he was healed?
options: Tell no man but show himself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded
Go and tell everyone what happened
Follow Jesus to the next town
Remain at home and rest
questions.correctAnswer: Tell no man but show himself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:4 records Jesus' instruction to the healed leper to tell no man, but to show himself to the priest and offer the gift commanded by Moses.

questions.question: Where did Jesus enter when the centurion came to him?
options: Capernaum
Jerusalem
Bethany
Nazareth
questions.correctAnswer: Capernaum
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:5 states that Jesus entered into Capernaum when the centurion came to him.

questions.question: What did the centurion say about his servant's condition?
options: My servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented
My servant is blind and cannot see
My servant is deaf and cannot hear
My servant is possessed by an evil spirit
questions.correctAnswer: My servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:6 states that the centurion said his servant lay at home sick of palsy and was grievously tormented.

questions.question: What did Jesus say to the centurion about healing his servant?
options: I will come and heal him
Your faith will make him well
Go and your servant will be healed
I will send my disciples to heal him
questions.correctAnswer: I will come and heal him
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:7 records Jesus saying to the centurion, 'I will come and heal him.'

questions.question: How did the centurion respond to Jesus' offer to come to his house?
options: Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed
Please come quickly and heal him in person
I will prepare a feast for you
Thank you, I will bring him to you
questions.correctAnswer: Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:8 shows the centurion humbly saying he is not worthy for Jesus to come under his roof but believes that Jesus' word alone will heal his servant.

questions.question: What illustration did the centurion use to explain his authority?
options: I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth
I am a shepherd and my sheep follow my voice
I am a king and my subjects obey my commands
I am a merchant and my workers do as I say
questions.correctAnswer: I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:9 records the centurion explaining his authority by saying he commands soldiers who obey his orders.

questions.question: What was Jesus' reaction when he heard the centurion's faith?
options: He marvelled and said he had not found so great faith in Israel
He was displeased and doubted the centurion
He immediately healed the servant without comment
He sent the servant to be healed by others
questions.correctAnswer: He marvelled and said he had not found so great faith in Israel
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:10 states that Jesus marvelled and said he had not found so great faith in Israel.

questions.question: Who did Jesus say shall come from the east and west to sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven?
options: Many
Few
Only Israelites
The Pharisees
questions.correctAnswer: Many
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:11 says that many shall come from the east and west and shall sit with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

questions.question: The children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness, where there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:12 states that the children of the kingdom will be cast out into outer darkness with weeping and gnashing of teeth.

questions.question: Jesus told the healed leper to offer the gift Moses commanded for a testimony unto them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:4 records Jesus instructing the leper to show himself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded as testimony.

questions.question: The centurion stated he was not worthy that Jesus should come under his roof but asked Him to only speak the word to heal his servant.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:8 shows the centurion said Jesus did not need to come to his house, just to speak the word to heal his servant.

questions.question: Jesus did not physically go to the centurion's house or touch the servant; He healed by speaking the word.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Though not explicitly stated in these verses, the centurion's faith was that Jesus could heal by speaking the word only (Matthew 8:8-9), and Jesus marvelled at this faith (Matthew 8:10). There is no mention of Jesus touching the servant.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus say to the centurion regarding his servant's healing?
options: Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee.
Your faith has made you whole.
I will come and heal him.
Thy servant is healed.
questions.correctAnswer: Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee.
questions.explanation: This is the exact statement made by Jesus to the centurion in Matthew 8:13, affirming that the centurion's belief was the basis for the healing.

questions.question: What does Matthew 8:13 promise will happen if someone believes as the centurion did?
options: They will be healed.
They will receive eternal life.
Their sins will be forgiven.
They will have peace.
questions.correctAnswer: They will be healed.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:13 indicates that belief leads to the fulfillment of desires, as demonstrated by the centurion's servant being healed.

questions.question: What did Jesus do when he saw Peter's mother-in-law sick?
options: He prayed for her.
He touched her hand, and the fever left her.
He commanded the fever to leave.
He went to find medicine.
questions.correctAnswer: He touched her hand, and the fever left her.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:15 describes Jesus touching her hand, which resulted in her fever leaving her.

questions.question: What does Matthew 8:14 indicate about Peter's mother-in-law's condition?
options: She was dead.
She was sick of a fever.
She was blind.
She was possessed.
questions.correctAnswer: She was sick of a fever.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:14 clearly states that Peter's mother-in-law was laid sick of a fever when Jesus entered the house.

questions.question: What action did many take when evening came, according to Matthew 8:16?
options: They brought food to Jesus.
They brought unto him many that were possessed with devils.
They left the city.
They built a shelter.
questions.correctAnswer: They brought unto him many that were possessed with devils.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:16 recounts how people brought those possessed by devils to Jesus for healing during the evening.

questions.question: What does Matthew 8:17 say was fulfilled through Jesus' actions?
options: He took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.
He taught the people to pray.
He performed miracles.
He preached the gospel.
questions.correctAnswer: He took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:17 mentions the fulfillment of the prophecy concerning Jesus taking upon himself our infirmities and sicknesses.

questions.question: When Jesus saw the great multitudes, what did he command according to Matthew 8:18?
options: He commanded them to follow him.
He gave commandment to depart unto the other side.
He told them to sit down.
He asked for their faith.
questions.correctAnswer: He gave commandment to depart unto the other side.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:18 states that upon seeing the great multitudes, Jesus instructed his followers to depart to the other side.

questions.question: What did the scribe offer to Jesus in Matthew 8:19?
options: To follow him whithersoever he goes.
To serve him as a disciple.
To provide for his needs.
To spread his teachings.
questions.correctAnswer: To follow him whithersoever he goes.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:19 reveals that a certain scribe expressed his desire to follow Jesus wherever he went.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about his living conditions in Matthew 8:20?
options: The Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
He lives in a house of many rooms.
He has a comfortable place to rest.
He sleeps under the stars.
questions.correctAnswer: The Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
questions.explanation: In Matthew 8:20, Jesus explains that unlike foxes and birds, he does not have a place to rest his head.

questions.question: What did another disciple request in Matthew 8:21?
options: To follow Jesus immediately.
To go and bury his father.
To stay behind with family.
To ask for a blessing.
questions.correctAnswer: To go and bury his father.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:21 records that another disciple asked Jesus if he could first go and bury his father.

questions.question: What was Jesus' response to the disciple in Matthew 8:22?
options: Let the dead bury their dead.
You are not worthy.
Follow me, and you will be blessed.
Your request is granted.
questions.correctAnswer: Let the dead bury their dead.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:22 shows Jesus instructing the disciple to follow him and let the dead take care of their own.

questions.question: What happened when Jesus entered a ship with his disciples in Matthew 8:23?
options: They encountered a storm.
They caught many fish.
They sang hymns.
They found peace.
questions.correctAnswer: They encountered a storm.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:23 indicates that after entering the ship, a great tempest arose in the sea.

questions.question: Did Jesus show concern for his disciples when the tempest arose?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In Matthew 8:24, it is noted that Jesus was asleep during the tempest, indicating a lack of immediate concern for the situation.

questions.question: Was the leper cleansed when he approached Jesus in Matthew 8:3?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:3 states that after Jesus touched the leper, he was immediately cleansed, affirming the leper's faith in Jesus' ability to heal.

questions.question: Did Jesus command the centurion to come to his house to heal his servant?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In Matthew 8:7, Jesus states he will come to heal the servant, but the centurion expresses unworthiness for Jesus to enter his house, leading Jesus to heal by word alone.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 8.

questions.question: In Matthew 8:25, what do the disciples say to Jesus when they awake Him during the storm?
options: Lord, save us: we perish.
Master, we are lost.
Save us, we are sinking.
Lord, calm the sea.
questions.correctAnswer: Lord, save us: we perish.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:25 records the exact words of the disciples: 'Lord, save us: we perish.'

questions.question: What question does Jesus ask His disciples in Matthew 8:26 after being awakened?
options: Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith?
Do ye not yet believe?
Who is this that even the winds obey him?
Where is your trust in God?
questions.correctAnswer: Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith?
questions.explanation: Jesus asks in Matthew 8:26, 'Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith?' addressing their doubt.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the men after Jesus calmed the storm in Matthew 8:27?
options: What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!
Truly, he is the Son of God.
Let us follow Him always.
This is a prophet sent from God.
questions.correctAnswer: What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:27 shows their marvel: 'What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!'

questions.question: In Matthew 8:28, where does Jesus go after crossing to the other side of the sea?
options: The country of the Gergesenes
The city of Capernaum
The hill country of Galilee
The valley of Jezreel
questions.correctAnswer: The country of the Gergesenes
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:28 states Jesus came into 'the country of the Gergesenes' after crossing over.

questions.question: What did the devils say to Jesus in Matthew 8:29?
options: What have we to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?
Depart from us, for we know who you are.
We recognize your power, but leave us be.
Are you here to save or to harm?
questions.correctAnswer: What have we to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?
questions.explanation: The devils cried out as recorded in Matthew 8:29 with this exact question.

questions.question: What happened to the herd of swine after the devils entered them, according to Matthew 8:32?
options: They ran violently down a steep place into the sea and perished.
They scattered across the fields and were lost.
They returned to their pens unharmed.
They were seized by the townspeople.
questions.correctAnswer: They ran violently down a steep place into the sea and perished.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:32 describes how the swine ran violently down a steep place into the sea and perished.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'epitrepo' (ἐπιτρέπω) in Matthew 8:31 mean?
options: Allow or permit
Cast out
Command
Refuse
questions.correctAnswer: Allow or permit
questions.explanation: In Matthew 8:31, 'epitrepo' means 'allow or permit,' as the devils ask Jesus to permit them to enter the swine.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Matthew 8:24-27 when describing the storm and Jesus’ calming of it?
options: Chiasm
Metaphor
Foreshadowing
Parallelism
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The passage in Matthew 8:24-27 uses a chiasm structure: the storm surrounding Jesus asleep (A), disciples’ fear (B), Jesus’ rebuke (C), calm (B'), and men marveling (A').

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed by Matthew 8:17, which speaks of Jesus bearing infirmities and sicknesses?
options: Isaiah 53:4
Psalm 23:4
Exodus 12:13
Deuteronomy 6:5
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 53:4
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:17 quotes Isaiah 53:4, which prophesies the suffering servant bearing our infirmities and sicknesses.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the theme of faith in authority as seen in Matthew 8:8-10?
options: Hebrews 11:1
James 2:19
Romans 10:17
Mark 11:22
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 11:1
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:1 defines faith as the assurance of things hoped for, connecting to the centurion’s faith in Jesus’ authority in Matthew 8:8-10.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus calming the storm in Matthew 8:24?
options: Jesus and His disciples enter a ship.
Jesus heals Peter’s mother-in-law.
Jesus teaches the multitudes on the mountain.
Jesus casts out devils.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus and His disciples enter a ship.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:23 records Jesus entering the ship with His disciples immediately before the storm arises in 8:24.

questions.question: How does the healing of the centurion’s servant in Matthew 8:13 demonstrate the concept of faith in Jesus’ word?
options: The servant was healed at that very hour because the centurion believed Jesus’ command without needing His presence.
Jesus physically visited the servant to heal him.
The centurion had to perform a ritual for healing to occur.
Faith was secondary to the servant’s own prayers.
questions.correctAnswer: The servant was healed at that very hour because the centurion believed Jesus’ command without needing His presence.
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:13 shows the servant healed immediately because the centurion trusted Jesus’ spoken word alone.

questions.question: What typological significance can be drawn from Jesus commanding the unclean spirits to enter the swine in Matthew 8:31-32?
options: It symbolizes the casting out of evil from humanity into unclean animals, representing the transfer of sin.
It foreshadows Jesus’ death and resurrection.
It illustrates the destruction of the temple.
It signifies the rejection of Gentiles.
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the casting out of evil from humanity into unclean animals, representing the transfer of sin.
questions.explanation: The transfer of demons into swine (unclean animals) in Matthew 8:31-32 typologically represents removal of evil from people, consistent with Jewish purity laws.

questions.question: How does the account of the two demon-possessed men in Matthew 8:28-34 reflect cultural and religious tensions of the time?
options: The presence of swine and the reaction of the local people highlight Jewish-Gentile boundaries and economic concerns.
It shows harmony between Jews and Gentiles.
It reflects Roman political control over the region.
It depicts the acceptance of demon possession as normal.
questions.correctAnswer: The presence of swine and the reaction of the local people highlight Jewish-Gentile boundaries and economic concerns.
questions.explanation: Swine were unclean to Jews (Matthew 8:30-34), so their loss caused fear and rejection of Jesus, illustrating cultural tensions.

questions.question: True or False: In Matthew 8:34, after witnessing the miracle, the whole city welcomed Jesus and asked Him to stay.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:34 states the city came out to meet Jesus but besought Him to depart from their coasts, not to stay.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 8:3 teach about God's nature?
options: God's willingness to heal and restore sinners
God's judgment on sin without mercy
God's detachment from human suffering
God's selective grace only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: God's willingness to heal and restore sinners
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:3 shows Jesus willingly touching and cleansing the leper, demonstrating God's compassionate and healing nature toward sinners.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 8:10 teach about faith and salvation?
options: Great faith is recognized and rewarded by God even outside Israel
Faith is irrelevant to God's healing power
Only ethnic Israelites can have saving faith
Faith guarantees immediate earthly prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Great faith is recognized and rewarded by God even outside Israel
questions.explanation: Jesus marvels at the centurion's faith, stating He has not found such faith even in Israel, highlighting the doctrine that faith is key to salvation and is not ethnically limited.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 8:22 teach about discipleship and priorities in the kingdom of God?
options: Following Jesus requires radical commitment, prioritizing Him over even family obligations
Family obligations must always take precedence over following Christ
Discipleship is optional and can wait until personal affairs are settled
The kingdom of God is primarily about social justice
questions.correctAnswer: Following Jesus requires radical commitment, prioritizing Him over even family obligations
questions.explanation: Jesus commands the disciple to "Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead," emphasizing the radical call to prioritize discipleship above natural ties.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 8:26 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty
Omniscience
Immutability
Justice
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: In Matthew 8:26, Jesus rebukes the winds and the sea, demonstrating His sovereign authority over creation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 8:17 specifically demonstrate?
options: Substitutionary atonement
Omnipresence
Holiness
Wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Substitutionary atonement
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:17 quotes Isaiah to show that Jesus 'bare our sicknesses,' indicating He took on human infirmities to atone for sin, reflecting substitutionary atonement.

questions.question: How does Matthew 8:11 connect to the broader theme of Gentile inclusion in the kingdom of God?
options: It anticipates Gentiles joining Israel's patriarchs in the kingdom
It limits the kingdom to ethnic Israel only
It predicts a future earthly kingdom ruled by Israelite kings
It suggests Gentiles will be subordinate to Israelites in the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates Gentiles joining Israel's patriarchs in the kingdom
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:11 speaks of 'many from the east and west' sitting with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, indicating Gentile inclusion in the kingdom, fulfilling God's promise to bless all nations.

questions.question: How does the healing of the centurion's servant (Matthew 8:5-13) relate to the theme of faith in Jesus' authority elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It exemplifies faith in Jesus' spoken word as authoritative and effective
It shows that physical proximity to Jesus is necessary for healing
It demonstrates that faith must be accompanied by ritual works
It indicates that only Jewish faith is acceptable
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies faith in Jesus' spoken word as authoritative and effective
questions.explanation: The centurion's faith in Jesus' word alone (Matthew 8:8-9) highlights the power of Jesus' authority, consistent with other Scripture where faith trusts God's word without requiring signs.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 8:12 and Matthew 8:11 teach about salvation and judgment?
options: Salvation is open to Gentiles by faith; judgment awaits those who reject the kingdom despite privilege
Salvation is by works; judgment is arbitrary
Only Jews will be saved; Gentiles are excluded
Judgment is only for non-believers outside the visible church
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is open to Gentiles by faith; judgment awaits those who reject the kingdom despite privilege
questions.explanation: Verse 11 promises many from east and west will join the patriarchs, while verse 12 warns that 'children of the kingdom' (Jews) will be cast out, teaching that faith, not ethnicity, determines salvation and judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 8:4 and Matthew 8:17 teach about Jesus' fulfillment of Old Testament law and prophecy?
options: Jesus fulfills the law's requirements and the prophetic role by healing and instructing obedience
Jesus abolishes the law and prophecy altogether
Jesus ignores the law's ceremonial ordinances
Jesus only fulfills prophecy but disregards the law
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus fulfills the law's requirements and the prophetic role by healing and instructing obedience
questions.explanation: Verse 4 instructs the healed leper to follow Mosaic law (show himself to the priest), and verse 17 cites Isaiah's prophecy fulfilled in Jesus' healing, showing fulfillment of law and prophecy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 8:20 and Matthew 8:22 teach about the cost of discipleship?
options: Discipleship requires forsaking earthly security and familial obligations
Discipleship guarantees earthly comfort and social status
Discipleship is primarily about religious rituals
Discipleship is optional and easily deferred
questions.correctAnswer: Discipleship requires forsaking earthly security and familial obligations
questions.explanation: Verse 20 highlights Jesus' homelessness, and verse 22 calls to leave burial duties, together emphasizing the radical cost and total commitment required for discipleship.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jesus' command to the sea to be still (Matthew 8:23-27) is mythological exaggeration. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It shows Jesus' divine authority over nature, authenticating His identity as Son of God
It is a poetic metaphor with no historical basis
It teaches that Jesus feared the storm like any human
It implies that natural disasters are random and uncontrollable
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Jesus' divine authority over nature, authenticating His identity as Son of God
questions.explanation: Verses 26-27 demonstrate Jesus rebuking the wind and sea, causing calm, which astonishes the disciples and reveals His divine sovereignty over creation.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 8:28-32 teach about the spiritual realm and Christ's authority over evil?
options: Jesus has authority over demonic powers and liberates those oppressed
Demons have ultimate control over the physical world
Jesus fears demonic powers and avoids confrontation
Spiritual oppression is unbreakable
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus has authority over demonic powers and liberates those oppressed
questions.explanation: The narrative shows Jesus casting out demons and commanding them, demonstrating His sovereign authority over evil spirits.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 8:4 specifically demonstrate?
options: Faithfulness to the covenant and Mosaic law
Wrath against sinners
Omnipresence
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness to the covenant and Mosaic law
questions.explanation: Jesus commands the healed leper to present himself to the priest and offer the commanded gift, showing His faithfulness to God's covenant law.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 8:7 specifically demonstrate?
options: Compassion
Jealousy
Omniscience
Wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Compassion
questions.explanation: Jesus' willingness to come and heal the centurion's servant shows His compassion for human suffering.

questions.question: How does Matthew 8:34 fit into the narrative arc of Jesus' ministry regarding rejection and acceptance?
options: It illustrates the common pattern of Jesus being rejected by towns despite His miracles
It shows universal acceptance of Jesus throughout Israel
It indicates Jesus' ministry was politically motivated
It depicts immediate establishment of Jesus' earthly kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the common pattern of Jesus being rejected by towns despite His miracles
questions.explanation: The crowd begs Jesus to leave after the demoniacs are healed, showing rejection despite His power, a theme repeated in the Gospels.
